name: X5105
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not a Xiegu publication and not affiliated with Xiegu.
verified: Compiled from the Xiegu X5105 Operation Manual version 3.0, September 2026. Not checked against a radio. The manual documents no factory reset and no repeater operation.
specs: 160 through 10 m, plus 6 m. Check the WARC bands on your own radio
CW, AM, USB, LSB, FM. The mode key cycles LSB, USB, CW, CW reverse, narrow FM and AM
5 W on SSB, CW and FM. 1.5 W AM carrier. Adjustable from 0.1 W
COM, also marked CIV, using the standard CI-V command set
keys: Long press to switch on or off. Held more than eight seconds it resets the controller, which is the recovery for a crash.
Short press steps to the next menu page.
Four keys that operate whatever the screen shows above each one.
Cycles LSB, USB, CW, CW reverse, narrow FM and AM.
Cycles preamp on, attenuator on, and both off.
Toggles the noise blanker. Long press switches the battery display between level and voltage.
Short press brings the tuner in line, an antenna icon appears. Hold about a second to tune.
Short press enters power setting, then the main knob, 0.1 to 5 W.
Swaps the VFOs. Long press copies the foreground VFO to the background.
Swaps VFO and memory. Long press while in memory writes the channel into the VFO.
The manual gives two conflicting accounts. Either short press locks and a one second press toggles the backlight, or long press locks and short press steps the backlight. Find out which yours does.
quick: AGC off, slow, fast or auto. RF gain. Squelch. Compression with its level.
Digital filter with low and high cut. Noise reduction with level. Notch with centre and bandwidth. Equaliser, bass, mid and treble.
Channel manager, preset messages, and the boot screen callsign.
Key type, sidetone, break-in time and break-in on or off. Iambic mode, keyer speed and dot to dash ratio in the submenu.
Data mode with PSK31. The scanning receiver. The standing wave sweep.
Mic selection and VOX. Speaker or earphone. Line gains. PTT mode.
filters: On or off, shaped by a low cut and a high cut. Xiegu prints no bandwidth figures.
Digital notch with a centre and a bandwidth.
On or off, with a level.
tasks: MENU to page 3, open the channel manager, select the channel number, save. Names are set the same way, stepping to the tag field and picking characters with the main knob.
V/M switches into memory mode. A long press of V/M in memory copies the channel into the VFO.
MENU to page 5, start the scanning receiver. Step is selectable at 0.5, 1, 2, 5 or 10 kHz, with pause and resume.
Short press Po, rotate the main knob, 0.1 to 5 W.
Short press ATU to bring it in line, hold about a second to tune. It returns to receive on its own.
MENU to page 5, standing wave sweep, with bandwidth, mode and speed options.
notes: Five watts and a built-in battery and tuner is the whole point of this radio. It is the one on this list that needs the least around it.
Xiegu documents no factory reset. Holding the power key more than eight seconds resets the controller after a crash, and that is all there is.
This is the only Xiegu on this list with a real receive scanner. The other two only sweep the antenna.
The manual disagrees with itself about the lock key. Try it once at home and cross out the wrong line above.
Xiegu's manual describes no repeater offset, shift, tone or tone squelch for this radio. It has FM but no documented repeater support, so nothing about working a repeater appears on this card.
control: COM, also marked CIV, standard CI-V command set
The supplied data cable, with its driver installed

ACC, 8-pin mini DIN, for computer audio in and out
